The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(3)$ where $h(x)=f(x)+g(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The addition rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)+{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(3)={f}^{′}(3)+{g}^{′}(3).
$$

Also, notice that $x=3$ corresponds to

- the interval $x\in (2,4)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (2.5,4)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14259483/assets/19a32fa6a7b2b6481052ab3539838bb00d486f92ea3f08b54efa2a1cfc69d221.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (2,4)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{0-2}{4-2}=-1.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(3)=-1.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (2.5,4)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{1-1}{4-2.5}=0.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(3)=0.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(3) & ={f}^{′}(3)+{g}^{′}(3) \\  & =-1+0 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14259483/assets/a074e2931c35862d5611cd3b2efe285144c7f85ce62b88278ee79851c8e40bf4.png)

Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(4)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(4)=\frac{{f}^{′}(4)\cdot g(4)-f(4)\cdot {g}^{′}(4)}{(g(4))^{2}}.
$$

From the graph above, we obtain that $f(4)=\frac{1}{2}$ and $g(4)=-\frac{1}{2}.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (3,5)$ equals $-\frac{3}{2}.$ So, ${f}^{′}(4)=-\frac{3}{2}.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (\frac{7}{2},5)$ equals $1.$ So, ${g}^{′}(4)=1.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(4) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(4)\cdot g(4)-f(4)\cdot {g}^{′}(4)}{{(g(4))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{3}{2})\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1}{{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{4})}{(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(-3)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(-3)=\frac{{f}^{′}(-3)\cdot g(-3)-f(-3)\cdot {g}^{′}(-3)}{(g(-3))^{2}}.
$$

From the graph above, we obtain that $f(-3)=-1$ and $g(-3)=-2.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-4,0)$ equals $1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-3)=1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (-4,4)$ equals $0.$ So, ${g}^{′}(-3)=0.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(-3) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-3)\cdot g(-3)-f(-3)\cdot {g}^{′}(-3)}{(g(-3))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot 0}{(-2)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${p}^{′}(1.5)$ where $p(x)=f(x)g(x).$

${p}^{′}(1.5)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The product rule for derivatives gives

$$
{p}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)+f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{p}^{′}(1.5)={f}^{′}(1.5)\cdot g(1.5)+f(1.5)\cdot {g}^{′}(1.5).
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(1.5)=-2$ and $g(1.5)=-0.5.$

Additionally,

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(1.5)=1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $1.$ So, ${g}^{′}(1.5)=1.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(1.5) & ={f}^{′}(1.5)\cdot g(1.5)+f(1.5)\cdot {g}^{′}(1.5) \\  & =1\cdot (-0.5)+(-2)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2.5.\end{aligned}
$$
